  "situation": "At night, the JTAC requested close air support from the ASOC, which said support could only be provided if a troops-in-contact (TIC) situation was declared based on an imminent threat. No own troops were physically in contact on the sandbank where two fuel tankers and an armed group were located. The commander believed a large armed group and fuel‑laden tankers a few kilometres away constituted an imminent threat to the PRT. The commander was aware that other German forces were engaged elsewhere and that the PRT had limited defensive capability. Under ISAF rules of engagement, a TIC could be declared either when troops are in direct fire or when an imminent threat exists. The commander considered that declaring a TIC would satisfy the ASOC requirement and enable air support to protect the PRT and civilians.",
